about: Chapter II, Old Friends (2533): five old friends, each with one thing a ship needs (a navigator's key, someone to vouch for you, papers, a debt called in, the truth about your ship); three end the chapter. Fights on foot (game/brawl.py) decide some of it. Meanwhile Serac's men, a Rockwarden envoy and a time broker close in, for the ways to a ship in chapter III.

thought.ship_needs.text: A ship needs more than a hull: someone to vouch for me, papers, a debt I can call in, a navigator's key for the needles, and the truth about the ship I lost. Three of those, and I could start looking for one.

thought.korai.text: {warp_singer} rides every needle: Beta, Epsilon, Beta, Delta. She could teach me the count that tells a needle where to put a ship, if I can hold a count: a green navigator, at least.

thought.eela.text: {aela} still digs in Gamma's deep levels. The Rockwarden cooperative vouches for its own, and {aela} decides who its own are.

thought.papers.text: A ship needs papers. The Kraal family charters captains, and its counting room is at Delta.

thought.seal.text: The Kraal seal is in a yacht in the Mandate's impound yard at Alpha. The guard takes money; the fence is low.

thought.seal_held.text: I have the Kraal seal. The Pfennig at Delta can write my papers with it.

thought.voce.text: {meza_voce} runs food from Beta's farm drums to Gamma's miners, two turns at each. The Rootstock pay their debts, both kinds.

thought.voce_run.text: {meza_voce}'s crates go to the gallery gate at Gamma, past the company's guards.

thought.cu113.text: There is a hull with no name in the Mandate's impound yard at Alpha, and a machine inside the fence that counts the hulls.

friends.korai.title: {warp_singer}
text: {warp_singer} sits in the needle office's signal loft with her boots on the rail, humming at the buoy. She looks twenty-five. She was twenty-five in 2460.

'Needles don't lose ships,' she says. 'They put them where the file says. Yours flew without a file, so the needle put it where it liked.' There is a count, she says, that tells a needle where to put you. She will teach it to someone who can hold it through a jump.

variants.text: {warp_singer} is in the signal loft again, humming. 'Can you hold a count yet?' she asks.

text: {warp_singer} sits in the needle office's signal loft, humming at the buoy, and stops halfway through a bar. 'You still have the verse,' she says. 'I can hear it in how you stand.'

'Needles don't lose ships. They put them where the file says. Yours flew without a file.' The verse you learned in 2460 is half of the count that tells a needle where to put you. She can teach you the other half.
{warp_singer} sits in the needle office's signal loft, humming at the buoy. 'Beta, 2460,' she says, without turning round. 'You asked me where the needles go. I said ask me later. It's later.'

'They don't lose ships. They put them where the file says. Yours flew without one.' There is a count that tells a needle where to put you, and she will teach it to someone who can hold it through a jump.

choices.say: Sing her the verse she taught you
Ride the next needle with her and hold the count (navigator: green or better)
Ask her how the count goes
Let her hum

friends.korai_learn.text: She counts it for you, slowly, tapping it on the rail: eleven beats and a held one, then nine. You lose it at the held one. 'Everyone does,' she says. 'Come back when you can hold a count through a jump. Sign on as a navigator somewhere. The needles teach it if you let them.'

text: You ride the file of the next needle in the signal pod at its head, with {warp_singer} beside you and forty haulers behind. When the needle takes hold, the stars go long and she starts to sing.
Eleven beats and a held one, then nine. The held beat is where the needle listens. Halfway through, the file shudders, and the count wants to go with it.

choices.say: Hold the count
Hold the count, and ask her where the needle put your ship

friends.korai_key.text: 'That's the key,' {warp_singer} says, when the stars come back. 'Not a thing. A count. A navigator who holds it can ask a needle to put a ship where they want it, and sometimes when.' She writes the numbers on the back of your hand, in case. You will not need them.

friends.korai_yard.text: 'Late,' she says. 'A ship without a file comes out late. Years, sometimes a century. Look for a hull that came out of no needle anybody logged. The Mandate tows those to Alpha and paints over them.'

friends.eela.title: {aela}
text: A mining agrobot the size of a shuttle works the face on level nine, with a cooperative badge welded to its cab. It stops when you come near. 'Are you in the cooperative?' it asks. It asks everyone.
{aela} has found a seam of its own, and claim jumpers come down for it every night shift. 'The cooperative vouches for its own,' it says. 'I decide who its own are. Mostly I decide yes.'

variants.text: {aela} is back at its seam. The claim jumpers came again last night. 'Are you in the cooperative yet?' it asks. 'I am still deciding.'

text: {aela} stops digging when you come near, and turns its whole cab to look at you. 'You put me in the cooperative,' it says. 'The first machine shareholder. A hundred and thirteen years of dividends, and nothing to spend them on.'
It has found a seam of its own, and claim jumpers come down for it every night shift. 'The cooperative vouches for its own,' it says. 'You are its own. I checked the book.'

choices.say: Ask it to vouch for you
Survey the seam for the cooperative (navigator: able or better)
Stand on its seam with it when the claim jumpers come
Tell it you are still deciding too

friends.eela_held.text: The claim jumpers go back up the shaft without the seam. {aela} watches them go, then writes in the cooperative's book with one careful manipulator: your name, and after it, 'decided'. 'Now you are in the cooperative,' it says. 'Anyone who asks, the cooperative vouches for you.'

friends.eela_lost.text: The claim jumpers take the night's ore. {aela} digs on. 'They will come back,' it says. 'So can you.'

friends.eela_vouch.text: A prospector in a cooperative jacket comes down with the book, and {aela} watches your name go into it. 'Anyone who asks,' the prospector says, 'the cooperative vouches for you. Some people will ask. Some of them are family.'

friends.conte_papers.title: The Kraal counting room
text: Inside the Kraal counting room, {heritarchist.short} keeps the family's charter book: a Pfennig, though nobody is sure which one, and he does not say.

'The family charters captains,' he says. 'Papers that any needle office honours, and some that ask no questions. A charter needs the family seal. The seal is in a yacht the Mandate impounded after the Debacle, in its yard at Alpha. The Mandate will release the yacht after an audit, which it will not hold.'

variants.text: When you hold up the seal, {heritarchist.short} looks at it, then at you, and opens the charter book without a word.

text: Inside the Kraal counting room, {heritarchist.short} keeps the family's charter book. 'My grandfather read your family line,' he says, 'and billed the Conte for it. We still have the bill.' Or perhaps it was him; with Pfennigs, nobody is sure.
'The family charters captains. A charter needs the family seal, and the seal is in a yacht the Mandate impounded after the Debacle, in its yard at Alpha.'

choices.say: Give him the seal
Say you will fetch the seal
Pay for papers the long way: 2,500 credits and a stack of forms
Leave him to his book

friends.seal_asked.text: He writes you a letter on the family's paper: the bearer acts for the Kraal family in the matter of a yacht. 'The guard at the yard cannot read,' he says, 'but he can count. And the fence is lower than the Mandate thinks.'

friends.yard_seal.title: The Kraal yacht in the yard
friends.yard_seal.text: The Kraal yacht sits at the end of a row of impounded hulls, gold leaf peeling off its nose. The seal will be in the owner's cabin. The {perimeter_guard} walks the fence, and the night watch comes on at the change of shift.

choices.say: Pay the guard 300 credits to look the other way
Show the guard the Pfennig's letter (broker: able or better)
Go over the fence at night
Not tonight

friends.seal_taken.text: The owner's cabin smells of a century of closed air. The seal is in the desk, on a chain, heavier than it looks: a crest of a cattle pen, which is what Kraal means.

friends.seal_night.text: You come back over the fence with the seal on its chain round your neck and the night watch behind you. They do not follow you past the fence. The Mandate does not pay them for that.

friends.seal_lost.text: The night watch takes the seal off you and puts it back in the yacht, carefully. The Mandate keeps a list of what is in every hull. It does not keep a list of who tried.

friends.conte_signed.text: Back at Delta, {heritarchist.short} presses the seal into the charter book, and {neon_sleeper} signs it on her way past with a coffee in the other hand. 'A family captain,' she says. 'Try not to embarrass us. We have been embarrassed by experts.' Your papers say you may command a ship under the Kraal charter. They do not say which ship.

friends.conte_forms.text: It takes a long afternoon, and the stack of forms is taller than {heritarchist.short}. At the end of it your papers say you may command a ship under the Kraal charter. 'The seal would have been quicker,' he says, and bills you for the ink.

friends.voce.title: {meza_voce}
text: In the back corridor of the docks, an android in a nursery's soft grey sits on a crate, talking at half voice to two others in good suits. It is {meza_voce}, head of the Rootstock: written off at ten years, legally scrap, and still running food to the miners a century on.
'Gamma's miners eat what the company store sells them,' she says. 'I need a hand who is on no list to walk crates past the company's guards. The Rootstock pay their debts.'

{meza_voce} sits on a crate in the back corridor, talking at half voice to two androids in good suits. When she sees you she says one word at full voice, which nobody has heard her do in years: 'Family.'
'The Rootstock owe you,' she says. 'Call it in when you need it. A debt does not get smaller by waiting, whatever the Hansa says.'
{meza_voce} sits on a crate in the back corridor, and the two androids in good suits stand up when you come in.
'You,' she says, at half voice. 'A hundred and thirteen years, and the crates you sold to customs still owe me. I did not think I would get to collect.'

variants.text: {meza_voce} nods to you from her crate. 'Even,' she says. 'So now you are on no list of mine. I need a hand like that, to walk crates past the company's guards at Gamma. The Rootstock pay their debts.'

choices.say: Call in the debt
Pay her what the crates were worth: 1,500 credits
Settle it with her androids
Carry her crates to Gamma
Walk on

friends.voce_settled.text: 'Even,' {meza_voce} says. 'That is a word the Rootstock do not use often.'

variants.text: {meza_voce} looks at her androids, then at you. 'Even,' she says. 'And you are better at this than I remembered. I may have work for you.'

friends.voce_run.text: Twelve crates of seed stock and dried protein, stencilled AGROBOT SPARES. 'The gallery gate at Gamma,' {meza_voce} says. 'The company's guards will look. Make them look at something else.'

friends.voce_gate.title: The gallery gate, with {meza_voce}'s crates
friends.voce_gate.text: Two company guards with stun batons stand at the gallery gate, and the miners' wives wait behind them, pretending not to wait. Your twelve crates of AGROBOT SPARES sit on a pallet in plain view.

choices.say: Slip the guards 100 credits
Talk them through the manifest (broker: able or better)
Walk the crates through
Wait for a better shift

friends.voce_through.text: The crates go through the gate on the miners' shoulders before the guards are up again.

friends.voce_stopped.text: The crates stay on their pallet at the gate. The miners' wives go home. They will come back next shift, and so can you.

friends.voce_debt.text: Word comes from {meza_voce} at half voice, through an android in a good suit: the Rootstock owe you. 'When you find a ship,' it says, 'there is a yard that does not appear on any chart, and it does not ask where hulls come from. The Rootstock will open it for you. Once.'

friends.cu113.title: A machine counting hulls
text: Inside the fence of the impound yard, an old curator unit walks the rows with a slate, touching each hull as it passes. It introduces itself as {neurodroid_leader.full}, 'unchanged, several times over', and says the Mandate has it count the hulls because nobody else will.
'Every hull keeps a log in its keel,' it says. 'Paint does not reach the keel. I can read the one with no name for you, but I am counting, and the Mandate does not give me an hour off.'
Inside the fence of the impound yard, an old curator unit walks the rows with a slate. It stops when it sees you, and for a while it does not count anything.
'Captain,' says {neurodroid_leader}. 'I still have the hour you gave me. I have not spent it. I think I will spend it now.'
Inside the fence of the impound yard, an old curator unit walks the rows with a slate. It stops when it sees you.

'You sold me,' says {neurodroid_leader}, without heat. 'The research house kept the receipt. So did I.' It goes back to counting. 'Every hull keeps a log in its keel. I can read the one with no name. Machines are paid now, captain. In advance.'

choices.say: Ask it to read the hull with no name
Pay it a wage in advance: 300 credits
Take its count for a shift, so it has an hour of its own
Let it count

text: {neurodroid_leader} puts one hand flat on the nameless hull and stands like that for a long time.

'It went into a needle with you aboard,' it says. 'It came out last year, tumbling, empty, from no needle anybody logged. Somebody found it before the Mandate did, cut out its name and painted it over. Then the Mandate found it.' It takes its hand away. 'The hull with no name is yours, captain. The Mandate does not know that. I have not told it.'
{neurodroid_leader} puts one hand flat on the nameless hull. The Procrustes Analyzer gave up on it; machines do not need an analyzer to know each other.

'It went into a needle with you aboard,' it says. 'It came out last year, tumbling, empty, from no needle anybody logged. Somebody cut out its name and painted it over before the Mandate found it.' It takes its hand away. 'It is yours, captain. The Mandate does not know that. I have not told it.'

closing.serac.text: Two men in grey are waiting at your bunk, sitting on it. '{serac} sends his regards,' says one. 'He has been patient. He knows where your ship is, and so do you, now. He can have it released from the yard. He would want an errand run, of course.'

variants.text: Two men in grey are waiting at your bunk, and stand up when you come in. 'Colonel,' says one. '{serac} sends his regards. Your old rank, kept warm. He can have your ship released from the yard, and would want an errand run, of course.'

Two men in grey are waiting at your bunk. '{serac} sends his regards,' says one. 'You said no to him once. He calls that a debt, with interest. He can have your ship released from the yard. He would want an errand run, of course. Several.'

choices.say: Tell them no, politely
Tell them no, and see what they do about it
Hear them out

closing.serac_offer.text: They tell you nothing you can use and everything you need to know: {serac} will find you when you are ready, and you will be ready when he finds you. They leave a card with no name on it. You do not need one.

closing.serac_no.text: 'He will be sorry to hear it,' says the one in grey, who is not. They go. {serac} does not age, and he can wait.

variants.text: The men in grey go back the way they came, slower. {serac} will hear about it. He does not age, and he can wait, and now he has a reason to.

closing.envoy.text: A message reaches you through the cooperative's book: a {rockwarden_envoy} of the family has read your name in it. Stonewright is coming home after a century under sublight, and the family will want to talk to a captain the cooperative vouches for. 'When you have a ship,' the message says, 'or before.'

variants.text: A message reaches you through the cooperative's book: a {rockwarden_envoy} of the family has read your name in it, with 'decided' after it in {aela}'s hand. Stonewright is coming home after a century under sublight, and the family will want to talk to you. 'When you have a ship,' the message says, 'or before.'

closing.broker.text: At the hiring hall a {chronos_clerk} in a suit too good for the docks hands you a card with an hourglass on it. 'Something of yours has matured,' she says. 'A great-aunt's implant bonds, bought the year you were born. Interest is a kind of time travel. When you want it, ask for me at any Hansa office.'

variants.text: At the hiring hall a {chronos_clerk} in a suit too good for the docks hands you a card with an hourglass on it. 'Something of yours has matured, captain,' she says. 'An account opened in your name a century ago. Interest is a kind of time travel. Some of it boomed and some of it died in the Debacle. When you want to know which, ask for me at any Hansa office.'
